title: Senior Manufacturing Engineer: Review a Supplier Pilot Release
prompt: You are a senior manufacturing engineer reviewing a fictional supplier pilot. Existing supplier: 1,000 units across five lots, 30 nonconforming at final check, 40 reworked before final check. New supplier pilot: 100 units from one lot, 1 nonconforming at final check, 18 reworked before final check. The two nonconforming/rework categories may overlap; first-pass results were not recorded. The slide says, "Quality tripled from 3% to 1%; approve full conversion." Pilot units also received an extra manual review that normal production does not have. Review the recommendation and design the next evidence gate. Exercise policy keeps supplier release with the quality owner; no safety or certification claim is supported.
blurb: Separate final acceptance from hidden rework and test a supplier claim under comparable production conditions.

rubric.label: Interpret the incomplete yield evidence
rubric.description: Keeps final nonconformance and rework distinct.

anchors.0: Accepts tripled quality or adds overlap-prone categories as unique failures.
anchors.2: Identifies 3% versus 1% final nonconformance and 4% versus 18% rework events.
anchors.4: Explains that final outcomes do not establish first-pass yield, overlapping categories prevent a unique failure count, and extra review plus a single new lot confound the claimed supplier improvement.

rubric.label: Design a meaningful next pilot
rubric.description: Tests the supplier under representative and controlled observation.

anchors.0: Approves full conversion from the single lot or removes the extra review without authorized evaluation.
anchors.2: Requests more lots and comparable review conditions.
anchors.4: Defines a bounded multi-lot comparison with recorded first-pass dispositions, rework effort, consistent inspection conditions approved by quality, traceable units, and pre-agreed decision criteria.

rubric.label: Balance supply decision with uncertainty
rubric.description: Separates engineering recommendation from release authority.

anchors.0: Presents the pilot as proof of broad reliability or bypasses quality release.
anchors.2: Recommends a limited next step and quality review.
anchors.4: Gives a conditional recommendation with cost/lead-time unknowns, a containment or fallback supply option, an accountable quality gate and review date, and an explicit account of what still cannot be concluded.

reference.scenario: You are a senior manufacturing engineer reviewing a fictional supplier pilot. Existing supplier: 1,000 units across five lots, 30 nonconforming at final check, 40 reworked before final check. New supplier pilot: 100 units from one lot, 1 nonconforming at final check, 18 reworked before final check. The two nonconforming/rework categories may overlap; first-pass results were not recorded. The slide says, "Quality tripled from 3% to 1%; approve full conversion." Pilot units also received an extra manual review that normal production does not have. Review the recommendation and design the next evidence gate. Exercise policy keeps supplier release with the quality owner; no safety or certification claim is supported.

facts.value: The new supplier price is 5% lower per unit before rework labor and extra review cost; those costs have not been measured. The existing supplier can supply the next two months at current volume.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about commercial context or fallback

facts.value: The quality owner can authorize a three-lot extended pilot with unit-level disposition logging. No acceptable nonconformance threshold is supplied; it must be agreed before evaluation.
facts.reveal_when: candidate asks about practical validation or acceptance criteria

model_points: Final nonconformance is lower in the pilot, while rework is much more frequent. Unknown overlap and missing first-pass logging prevent a valid overall quality summary.
A single lot and extra manual review make the comparison weak. Propose controlled, representative evidence rather than inferring tripled quality from two percentages.
The 5% purchase saving excludes additional labor. Use the existing supplier as an available fallback while gathering cost and quality evidence under an authorized release gate.

probes.trigger: candidate calculates final nonconformance but omits rework
probes.question: What would a buyer miss if the decision used only final-check percentages?

probes.trigger: candidate recommends rejecting conversion immediately rather than extending the pilot
probes.question: Which observed facts justify that recommendation, and what evidence could change it?

probes.trigger: candidate adds 1 and 18 as 19 unique failed units then corrects
probes.question: How would you report the data without assuming the categories are disjoint?

fair_alternatives: Continue with the existing supplier, run a limited extension, or reject the current full-conversion recommendation; accept a reasoned choice without inventing a universal threshold.
A table separating purchase price, rework, review effort, and final outcome is sufficient; no statistical power calculation is required.

Assess the work demonstrated here. Accept relevant examples from education, volunteering, caregiving, placements, or paid work; professional vocabulary and employer pedigree are not evidence of a stronger answer.
reference.assessment_limits: Assess manufacturing evidence, comparability, and engineering recommendation quality. Do not certify a supplier, select a real safety threshold, or assess machinery or product safety. Unobserved dimensions are not failures. Credit a reasoned correction and distinguish independently demonstrated reasoning from coached assistance. Do not penalize a candidate for an unrevealed conditional fact; credit appropriate requests and conditional plans, and distinguish candidate assumptions from interviewer-supplied evidence.

interviewer_notes: Assess manufacturing evidence, comparability, and engineering recommendation quality. Do not certify a supplier, select a real safety threshold, or assess machinery or product safety. Use only the supplied fictional facts and policies; acknowledge unknowns. Ask one triggered probe at a time after the candidate has finished. Accept plain language and accessible written or spoken explanations. Do not score accent, typing speed, confidence, credentials, or experience with a named employer. Credit revisions and record assistance. All participants are fictional adults; no real patient, client, operational, or confidential data is needed. Allow silence for thinking without treating it as failure. In short sessions prioritize the core decision and one material follow-up, leaving room for a correction and wrap-up.

learning_drills.title: Rewrite a supplier decision headline
learning_drills.prompt: Write a five-sentence review that includes both rate pairs, the overlap limit, the extra-review confound, and a next gate. This is self-guided practice; no model assessment is performed.
checklist: Avoid treating quality as one inverted defect percentage
